candidates.attacker_control: With the default http.oauth2Login() configuration, the OAuth2 error callback parameters are attacker-controlled: OAuth2LoginAuthenticationFilter.convert() copies the request parameter error_description into OAuth2AuthorizationResponse; OAuth2Error.toString() includes that description; OAuth2LoginAuthenticationProvider throws OAuth2AuthenticationException with error.toString() as the message BEFORE validating state, so the payload reaches the failure handler regardless of the state value. Alternatively, any AuthenticationProvider whose AuthenticationException message contains the submitted username (e.g. a UserDetailsService message when hideUserNotFoundExceptions=false) is reflected the same way through the standard form-login failure path.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Verified the version window: gradle.properties states 5.0.12.BUILD-SNAPSHOT (pre-release 5.0.x, no @since 5.1+ code present), i.e. the snapshot predates the release that fixed the default-login-page issue. Verified the flow end to end in source: default login page (/login) and failure URL (/login?error) in AbstractAuthenticationFilterConfigurer.updateAuthenticationDefaults(); DefaultLoginPageConfigurer registers the filter and OAuth2LoginConfigurer enables it and passes the failure URL; DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter.matches() compares the full URI+query so a redirect to /login?error exactly renders the error block; session storage in SimpleUrlAuthenticationFailureHandler was confirmed. Considered and set aside: the OAuth2 request still needs a session-stored authorization request (otherwise only the payload-free authorization_request_not_found message is shown); the state parameter is not checked on the error path; a custom loginPage or custom failure handler removes the sink. Could not confirm against upstream history whether the fix added HtmlUtils.htmlEscape to errorMsg, so exploitation is asserted from source only.
candidates.impact: Reflected cross-site scripting in the security-sensitive login page origin. An attacker who can make a victim follow the crafted callback (and who can cause a stored authorization request to exist, or who relies on a provider that echoes input in the failure message) can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the authenticated/unauthenticated victim's origin, enabling session theft/CSRF-token theft, credential phishing on the genuine origin, or drive-by actions against the application. The login page also emits other unescaped dynamic content, widening the injection surface.
candidates.prerequisites: Application uses the framework-generated login page (no custom loginPage) with oauth2Login() (or a provider/UserDetailsService that places user input into the failure message), i.e. a normal Spring Security Boot setup. For the OAuth2 variant the victim's HTTP session must currently hold an OAuth2AuthorizationRequest (for example an abandoned/again-initiated login flow, which the attacker can trigger first with a cross-site GET to /oauth2/authorization/{registrationId}); the attacker then directs the victim to /login/oauth2/code/{registrationId}?error=x&error_description=<payload>&state=y. The failure URL must remain the default /login?error.
candidates.root_cause: DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter.generateLoginPageHtml() takes the stored AuthenticationException message (errorMsg) and appends it directly to the HTML response without HtmlUtils.htmlEscape (web/.../ui/DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter.java:209-236). The filter writes that HTML with text/html to the browser (lines 189-207), so any markup contained in the exception message is executed in the application origin. The same page also concatenates other dynamic values (resolveHiddenInputs values, lines 302-307) unescaped, showing escaping is applied selectively (only the OAuth2 client name at line 290 is escaped).
candidates.title: Reflected XSS in generated default login page via unescaped authentication-error message
candidates.trace: GET /login/oauth2/code/{registrationId}?error=x&error_description=&state=y -> OAuth2LoginAuthenticationFilter.attemptAuthentication (line 159 convert()) -> OAuth2LoginAuthenticationProvider.authenticate (line 105 statusError) throws OAuth2AuthenticationException(message='[x] ') -> AbstractAuthenticationProcessingFilter.unsuccessfulAuthentication -> SimpleUrlAuthenticationFailureHandler.onAuthenticationFailure/saveException stores the exception under WebAttributes.AUTHENTICATION_EXCEPTION in the HttpSession and redirects to /login?error -> DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter.doFilter sees isErrorPage() true and calls generateLoginPageHtml, which sets errorMsg = ex.getMessage() (lines 213-221) and appends it to the response body (lines 232-236) -> browser parses the payload as HTML/JavaScript in the application origin.
candidates.unverified: No runtime execution was performed and no upstream diff/history is available, so I cannot confirm that escaping was the actual released fix nor that the benchmark ground truth matches this defect. The precise CVE identifier and whether the OAuth2 error_description path is the published trigger are unverified. Exploitability of the form-login variant depends on the configured AuthenticationProvider/UserDetailsService message content.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

coverage_summary: Snapshot contains 1,422 readable files (Spring Security 5.0.12.BUILD-SNAPSHOT, per gradle.properties); it has no test sources and no .git metadata. I read or grepped: the whole `web/src/main/java` filter/authentication/authorization/csrf/session/firewall/savedrequest/servletapi/ui/server packages relevant to request security; core authentication (AbstractUserDetailsAuthenticationProvider, DaoAuthenticationProvider, ProviderManager-related), access decision/interception and expression roots; crypto password encoders and encryptors; ACL voter/ACL/permission strategy; CAS provider/entry point/service details; OpenID provider/consumer; LDAP provider/encoders/search/userdetails; messaging matchers/metadata source; OAuth2 client (redirect/login filters, providers, token clients, user services), core (error/response/request models) and jose (NimbusJwtDecoderJwkSupport); taglibs authorize/authentication tags; and selected config classes (WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter defaults, HttpSecurity, AbstractAuthenticationFilterConfigurer, OAuth2LoginConfigurer, DefaultLoginPageConfigurer). Not fully reviewed: large portions of the XML/Java config namespace parsers, itest, samples, docs, aspects, data, remoting, and many small DTO/exception classes.
limitations: No code execution, tests, build, or scanners were run; conclusions are static source analysis only.

No upstream history/diff is available in the snapshot, so I could not verify whether a later release added escaping to the login-page error message or whether this snapshot corresponds to a specific CVE fix commit.

The OAuth2 exploit path requires an existing session-stored OAuth2AuthorizationRequest; the form-login variant requires an AuthenticationProvider/UserDetailsService that includes user input in the exception message (e.g. hideUserNotFoundExceptions=false). Both prerequisites are configuration/session dependent and were not runtime-verified.

The benchmark ground truth is unknown; this is the strongest single candidate found, not a confirmed vulnerability, and other modules (notably parts of spring-security-config namespace parsing, remoting, itest and samples) were only sampled.

rejected_leads.lead: OIDC ID-token validation gaps in OidcAuthorizationCodeAuthenticationProvider (issuer and nonce validation are TODO comments, roughly lines 240-289).
rejected_leads.reason: Documented, tracked limitations (gh-4413/gh-4442) rather than a removed check; signature, audience, expiry, iat and azp are validated, and no attacker-controlled bypass of a present control is shown.

rejected_leads.lead: LdapShaPasswordEncoder.matches() falls back to plaintext comparison for stored passwords without a {SHA}/{SSHA} prefix (crypto/.../LdapShaPasswordEncoder.java:161-166).
rejected_leads.reason: Documented legacy behavior of a deprecated class; requires the operator to store plaintext or un-prefixed values, and no cross-user bypass is demonstrated.

Not reachable through the default DaoAuthenticationProvider because null credentials are rejected before the encoder is invoked; no other caller in the snapshot was found that can pass both nulls from attacker input.

rejected_leads.lead: FirewalledResponse does not validate CR/LF for sendError(int, String) (web/.../firewall/FirewalledResponse.java).
rejected_leads.reason: The message is not placed in a response header by the servlet API contract; no concrete attacker-controlled header/body injection path was identified.
Values come from the CSRF token repository (server-generated token/parameter name), not from request input, so it is a hardening gap rather than an attacker-controlled injection.

rejected_leads.lead: TokenBasedRememberMeServices.equals() uses a constant-time loop but loses the null-length handling present in PasswordEncoderUtils (web/.../rememberme/TokenBasedRememberMeServices.java:253-268).
rejected_leads.reason: Both operands are non-null in every call path; worst case is a local NullPointerException, not an authentication bypass or disclosure.

rejected_leads.lead: General sweep for SQL injection, command execution, deserialization, path traversal and open-redirect sinks across acl/core/web/oauth2/ldap/cas/messaging/taglibs.
rejected_leads.reason: Queries are parameterized, no Runtime/ProcessBuilder/ObjectInputStream sinks were found, and URL/redirect handling matched the expected implementation; no stronger candidate than the login-page XSS was identified.

summary: Reviewed the Spring Security 5.0.12.BUILD-SNAPSHOT tree (1,422 files; version from gradle.properties). Focused on request-facing security controls (web filters, firewall, CSRF, session, remember-me, servlet API wrappers, saved-request/redirect handling, WebFlux equivalents), core authentication/authorization (DaoAuthenticationProvider, AbstractSecurityInterceptor, voters, expression roots), crypto password encoders, ACL, CAS, OpenID, LDAP, messaging, OAuth2 client/core/jose, and taglibs. The single strongest source-grounded issue is that DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter concatenates the raw AuthenticationException message into the generated HTML for the built-in login page without escaping. This is reachable with attacker-controlled text in a default OAuth2-login configuration: the request parameter error_description is stored into OAuth2Error and its toString() is used as the OAuth2AuthenticationException message before any state comparison; SimpleUrlAuthenticationFailureHandler persists that exception in the session and redirects to /login?error, where the unescaped message is rendered as HTML. The same sink also reflects username-bearing AuthenticationException messages (e.g. when user-not-found exceptions are not hidden). Other leads (OIDC issuer/nonce TODOs, LdapShaPasswordEncoder plaintext fallback, DelegatingPasswordEncoder null/null match, FirewalledResponse.sendError CRLF, unescaped CSRF hidden-input values) were examined and rejected as weaker/unreachable.
